body.en: The gradient of a curve from first principles, the power rule for differentiation, and reversing it to integrate.

\( \dfrac{d}{dx}x^{n}=nx^{n-1} \); the gradient at a point is the value of \( \tfrac{dy}{dx} \) there. Integration reverses this: \( \displaystyle\int x^{n}\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C \) for \( n\neq-1 \).

body.en:
Algebraic preparation: Express all algebraic fractions and surds in index form before differentiating or integrating: \(\frac{3}{x^2} = 3x^{-2}\), \(4\sqrt{x} = 4x^{1/2}\), \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2}\). Differentiating denominators directly without rewriting produces invalid derivatives.

Tangent vs Normal: The tangent line has gradient \(m_{\text{tan}} = \frac{dy}{dx}\). The normal line is perpendicular, having gradient \(m_{\text{norm}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{tan}}}\). Both lines pass through the exact same point \((x_1, y_1)\) on the curve.

Area between curves: Area is \(\int_a^b (y_{\text{top}} - y_{\text{bottom}})\,dx\). If a curve crosses the \(x\)-axis within the limits of integration, integrating across the roots will result in positive and negative areas cancelling out. You must integrate each section separately and sum the positive areas.

label.en: Worked Example C — Instantaneous Rate of Change & Tangent Line

body.en:
Let \( f(x) = 4x^3 - x^2 + 4 \). Find the instantaneous rate of change \( f'(9) \).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Differentiate term-by-term using the power rule: \( f'(x) = 12x^2 - 2x \).
  2. Substitute \( x = 9 \): \( f'(9) = 12(9)^2 - 2(9) = 972 - 18 = \mathbf{954} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Instantaneous Rate of Change & Tangent Line

body.en:
Let \( f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 + 4 \). Find the instantaneous rate of change \( f'(5) \).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Differentiate term-by-term using the power rule: \( f'(x) = 15x^2 - 2x \).
  2. Substitute \( x = 5 \): \( f'(5) = 15(5)^2 - 2(5) = 375 - 10 = \mathbf{365} \).

question.en: A curve has equation \(y = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x + 1\). (a) Find the coordinates of both stationary points. (b) Determine the nature of each stationary point using the second derivative \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\).
Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the curve \(y = 4x - x^2\) and the line \(y = x\).

solution.en:
Find points of intersection: \[4x - x^2 = x \Rightarrow 3x - x^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x(3 - x) = 0\] The curves intersect at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\). Between \(0\) and \(3\), the curve \(y = 4x - x^2\) lies above the line \(y = x\).
The enclosed area is: \[A = \int_0^3 \left[(4x - x^2) - x\right]\,dx = \int_0^3 (3x - x^2)\,dx\] Integrate: \[A = \left[\dfrac{3x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = \left(\dfrac{3(9)}{2} - \dfrac{27}{3}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{27}{2} - 9 = \dfrac{27 - 18}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2} = 4.5\]

question.en: Find the equation of the normal to the curve \(y = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{x}} + 2x\) at the point where \(x = 4\).

solution.en:
Rewrite in index form: \(y = 4x^{-1/2} + 2x\).
At \(x = 4\): \(y = 4(4^{-1/2}) + 2(4) = 4\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) + 8 = 2 + 8 = 10\). Point of contact is \((4, 10)\).
Differentiate: \[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\right) + 2 = -2x^{-3/2} + 2 = -\dfrac{2}{x^{3/2}} + 2\] At \(x = 4\): \(x^{3/2} = (\sqrt{4})^3 = 8\). Thus: \[m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{2}{8} + 2 = -\dfrac{1}{4} + 2 = \dfrac{7}{4}\] The normal has gradient \(m_{\text{norm}} = -\dfrac{1}{7/4} = -\dfrac{4}{7}\).
Using point \((4, 10)\): \[y - 10 = -\dfrac{4}{7}(x - 4) \Rightarrow 7(y - 10) = -4(x - 4) \Rightarrow 7y - 70 = -4x + 16 \Rightarrow 4x + 7y - 86 = 0\]

question.en: [Differentiation & Integration · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
